canonicalName: Type 2 Diabetes

properties.name: Type 2 Diabetes

canonicalName: Prediabetes

properties.name: Prediabetes
properties.definition: If your blood glucose levels are higher than the target range, but not high enough to be diagnosed with diabetes, doctors will diagnose you with prediabetes. Having prediabetes is serious because it raises the chance of developing type 2 diabetes.

canonicalName: Fasting Plasma Glucose Test

properties.name: Fasting Plasma Glucose Test
properties.definition: The fasting plasma glucose (FPG) test measures your blood glucose level at a single point in time. For the most reliable results, your doctor will give you the test in the morning after you have fasted for at least 8 hours. Fasting means having nothing to eat or drink except sips of water.

quote: The fasting plasma glucose (FPG) test measures your blood glucose level at a single point in time. For the most reliable results, your doctor will give you the test in the morning after you have fasted for at least 8 hours. Fasting means having nothing to eat or drink except sips of water.

canonicalName: A1C Test

properties.name: A1C Test
properties.definition: The A1C test is a blood test that provides your average levels of blood glucose over the last 3 months. Other names for the A1C test are hemoglobin A1C, HbA1C, glycated hemoglobin, and glycosylated hemoglobin test. You can eat and drink before this test. Before using the A1C test to diagnose diabetes, your doctor will consider factors, such as whether you are in your second or third trimester of pregnancy or whether you have certain types of anemia NIH external link or another problem with your blood.1 The A1C test might not be accurate in those cases.

canonicalName: A1C test in presence of hemoglobin variants

properties.triggerCriteria: you have certain types of hemoglobin, called hemoglobin variants
properties.rationale: Certain types of hemoglobin, called hemoglobin variants, can interfere with measuring A1C levels. Most A1C tests used in the United States are not affected by the most common variants. If your A1C test results and blood glucose levels do not match, your doctor should consider that the A1C test may not be a reliable test for you.
